topic: The AMD llama.cpp fork story: community patch set, retired AMD repo, Radeon options
title: The AMD fork that is not from AMD
description: The AMD llama.cpp fork everyone is sharing is not AMD's. AMD's own fork is retired, and the trending speedup is one maintainer's nineteen-patch set for stock llama.cpp. You'll learn what stock llama.cpp already does on Radeon via HIP and Vulkan, and what the patch set really adds. (Narration is AI-generated.)

narration_full: Your feed's AMD fork isn't from AMD. llama.cpp is the free program that runs AI models on your PC. Everyone's sharing it as AMD's own fork, its own in-house copy, for Radeon. What trended is a solo maintainer's patch set: nineteen code changes on a pinned copy. AMD's own fork is retired; its page says use the original. The original already runs on Radeon; AMD posts ready-made Windows downloads. A single machine backs the speedup. One user measured thirty-five tokens a second on his R-nine-seven-zero-zero. After patching, he reports fifty-five tokens a second, warning your mileage may vary. The Radeon fix in your feed came from a stranger, not AMD.
